scene.note: Rounding, sums and chance come from Python's own modules, and every draw can be made again from its seed.

steps.note: The base, a team out of range and how far a hand radio reaches go in.
The straight distance comes from a square root, and is divided by the reach.
Rounded up, it tells Rhona how many people to stand in the line.
A team's position and the size of a search square go in.
Each part is divided by the size and rounded down, west and south of the base too.
Rhona gets the square on the board the team is in.
The hours of the year's callouts go in, in any order.
The statistics module works out the mean and the median.
Rhona sees what a typical callout costs, with and without the long ones pulling it up.
The volunteers and a seed go in.
The seed sets where the chance starts, and a copy of the list is shuffled.
Every volunteer is on the rota once, and the same seed draws the same rota in front of everyone.
The volunteers, the nights of the week and a seed go in.
The seed is set once, then one driver is drawn from the whole list for each night.
Rhona gets a driver for every night, the same ones each time she draws with that seed.
